title: Grateful Dead Live at Old Renaissance Faire Grounds on 1972-08-27
source: (SET I and II) SBD > Re-Mixed Master RTR > DAT > SSSB.   (SET III) SBD > Re-Mixed Master RTR > PCM (via analog inputs and outputs) > DAT > SSSB

ai_review.summary: Warm, crystal‑clear soundboard captures a high‑energy 8/27/72 show with smoking Playing in the Band, soaring Dark Star and stellar He's Gone.
ai_review.review: The serafin SBD source delivers an ultra‑warm, well‑balanced mix that lets every instrument shine—even the stage banter feels like part of the experience. Musically the concert erupts after a modest first set, with a second‑set surge highlighted by a smoking Playing in the Band, a spacey Dark Star and powerhouse versions of He's Gone and Jack Straw, while the third set keeps the momentum high with Bird Song, Greatest Story Ever Told and a soulful Sing Me Back Home. A few reviewers note song splits and frequent announcements, but overall the performance is regarded as one of ’72’s finest.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both the musical energy and the warm soundboard mix; only a few low‑star comments mention minor annoyances, yielding an overall strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Super warm‑sounding SBD with crisp clarity; some listeners note split‑song edits and frequent stage announcements, but the mix is generally praised as beautiful and well balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set serves as a warm‑up; the second set takes off with high‑energy jams and becomes the show’s centerpiece, while the third set maintains momentum despite frequent banter. Overall flow is praised even though stage announcements can be distracting.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone described as warm, on the edge of a melt‑down and his vocals on Sing Me Back Home noted as especially sweet.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass highlighted for an unusually dynamic, funky jam and is often up in the mix during the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s stage banter and vocal intros add character; his voice carries a slight ping‑pong echo that places the listener right between stage and woods.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are praised as “very on” and contribute jazzy, spacey textures throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is described as fierce and driving, especially during the high‑intensity jams.
